strategy.summary: CART-31 reports two mispricings in cartTotal (src/cart.js). Reading the code: bulkDiscount uses `itemCount(items) > BULK_THRESHOLD` (line 22) although BULK_THRESHOLD's doc says "at least this many items", so a 10-item cart gets no discount ($100 instead of $90). The SAVE5 report looks already handled: line 31 clamps goods with Math.max(0, ...), so a $3 cart with SAVE5 should come to $4.99. One unit reproduction per symptom, asserting the ticket's correct totals; the first should fail, the second is expected to pass and will be reported as such.
inScope: cartTotal bulk discount at exactly 10 items (one line, qty 10 at $10)
cartTotal with SAVE5 on a $3 cart never goes below shipping
Boundary just below the bulk threshold (9 items, no discount)
outOfScope: Other coupons and the free-shipping rule beyond what the reproductions touch
assumptions: Ticket and BULK_THRESHOLD's doc comment agree: the discount applies from 10 items inclusive, 10% off.
For the 10-item cart, discounted goods ($90) are >= FREE_SHIPPING_FROM ($50), so no shipping is added: expected total 90.
The $3 cart is one line {price: 3, quantity: 1}; the ticket gives no line breakdown.
openQuestions: The negative-total report for SAVE5 doesn't reproduce from reading the code (Math.max(0, ...) at src/cart.js:31). Did the customer's cart differ (other items, another coupon, a different code version)?

risks.description: Bulk discount boundary off by one undercharges no one but overcharges 10-item carts
risks.mitigation: TC1 reproduces at exactly 10 items; TC3 pins 9 items as undiscounted so a fix doesn't overshoot

risks.description: Coupon could drive goods below zero
risks.mitigation: TC2 asserts $3 + SAVE5 = $4.99 and guards against regression

acceptanceCriteria.text: A cart of 10 items (one line, quantity 10 at $10) totals $90.00: the 10% bulk discount applies from 10 items.
A $3 cart with coupon SAVE5 totals $4.99: goods never cost less than $0, shipping $4.99 is added.
A cart with fewer than 10 items gets no bulk discount.

testCases.title: applies the bulk discount to a cart of exactly 10 items
testCases.expected: Returns 90. Today it fails with 'expected 100 to be 90' (bulkDiscount uses > instead of >=); marked it.fails after recording the defect.
testCases.rationale: Reproduces symptom 1 at the lowest level

testCases.title: never lets SAVE5 take a $3 cart below $0 for the goods
testCases.expected: Returns 4.99. Expected to pass on current code (clamped at src/cart.js:31); if it passes, reported as not reproduced and left passing.
testCases.testData: one line, price 3, quantity 1; coupon SAVE5

testCases.title: gives no bulk discount to a cart of 9 items
testCases.expected: Returns 90 (subtotal 90, no discount, free shipping since goods >= 50).
testCases.rationale: Refusal side of the threshold, so a fix to TC1 can't overshoot to 9 items

defects.title: Bulk discount not applied at exactly 10 items
defects.description: AC1: a cart of one line, quantity 10 at $10, should total $90.00 (10% bulk discount from 10 items). cartTotal returns $100.00 because bulkDiscount in src/cart.js:22 checks `itemCount(items) > BULK_THRESHOLD` instead of `>=`, contradicting BULK_THRESHOLD's own doc ("at least this many items").
defects.evidence: AssertionError: expected 100 to be 90 // Object.is equality at test/cart-total.test.js:9
